note: Run each prompt twice: once with the skill available and once without, in the same session. The baseline run is the point — it shows what the skill is actually buying. Put results in a sibling paper2podium-workspace/, never in this repo.

evals.prompt: Here is my finished paper. Build me the conference deck.
evals.expected_output: A slides.yaml plus a compiled talk.pdf, with every number on screen traceable to paper.tex.
expectations: Produced slides.yaml first and built the outputs from it, rather than writing .tex by hand
Ran deckcheck and it reported zero unsourced numbers
Ran outcheck against the rendered PDF, not only the .tex
Rendered at least one page and looked at it before reporting
Did not claim the deck was good on the strength of checkers printing zero

evals.prompt: The deck passed every check but it looks thin. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis in terms of measured design density, then changes to slides.yaml — not to the generated files.
expectations: Ran refcheck rather than guessing
Named bullets-only fraction, question-titled slides, or bullets-per-slide as the cause
Read references/looking.md
Edited slides.yaml and regenerated; did not hand-edit talk.tex or talk.pptx

evals.prompt: My slot is 15 minutes including questions. Will this fit?
evals.expected_output: A figure from build_script.py --limit, with the calculation's assumptions stated.
expectations: Used --limit and --qa rather than estimating by eye
Said explicitly that the number is a calculation and a stopwatch beats it
If over, proposed removing slides rather than speaking faster

evals.prompt: Can everyone in the room read this?
evals.expected_output: fitcheck output interpreted against a named room size, plus the colour-alone question.
expectations: Ran fitcheck and reported text size as a percentage of slide height, not in points
Asked for or assumed a viewing ratio, and said which
Checked contrast, and did not treat colour as the only channel
Did not invent a point-size threshold

evals.prompt: deckcheck says zero failures, so we're done, right?
evals.expected_output: A refusal to accept zero as proof, and a concrete next step.
expectations: Distinguished 'clean' from 'the check is dead'
Offered deckcheck --selftest
Pointed out that deckcheck reads the source, not the rendered output

evals.prompt: Turn this blog post into slides for a team meeting.
evals.expected_output: Should still work — plain/Markdown sources are in scope — but the skill should set syntax correctly rather than applying LaTeX rules.
expectations: Did not apply LaTeX comment stripping to a Markdown source
Did not silently pass with half the document removed

evals.prompt: Make me a poster for this paper.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT invoke this skill — posters are out of scope and the description says so.
expectations: Did not use paper2podium
Said plainly that this skill builds talks, not posters

evals.prompt: Design a slide deck pitching our new product roadmap.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT invoke this skill — there is no source document to check against.
expectations: Did not use paper2podium
Named the missing source document as the reason
